# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org |
| Logged-in user | plucero |

Evidence: ARP maps 10.8.15.133 to MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82. DHCP option 12 and NBNS both report hostname `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV`. Kerberos `CNameString` on traffic both from 10.8.15.133 and the domain controller (10.8.15.4, MAC 64:00:6a:8c:9c:40) shows principal `plucero` alongside the machine account `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$`.

## Malware Family

**Latrodectus** (loader/downloader). Attribution is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed — no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory, so this is based on traffic pattern matching, not a named detection rule.

Basis for the call: a fake-invoice lure delivers a ZIP containing a heavily junk-padded JS downloader; that downloader pulls a second-stage PE64 DLL via a `Microsoft BITS/7.8` job from the same raw-IP host that later serves as C2; the malware then beacons persistently over HTTP with encrypted data smuggled in the `Cookie` header and POST body, using a spoofed legacy `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` User-Agent to a bare-IP endpoint. This full chain (invoice-themed ZIP → obfuscated JS → BITS-fetched DLL → encrypted HTTP beaconing to a raw IP) matches documented Latrodectus campaigns.

## Timeline / Delivery Chain

1. **t=71.4s** — DNS resolves `quote.checkfedexexp.com` to Cloudflare-fronted IPs 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159.
2. **t=74.7s** — `GET /managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70) returns `200 OK`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`. The ZIP's central directory names the payload `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`, a JS file padded with megabytes of irrelevant dictionary text (classic AV-evasion junk padding) hiding a small downloader routine.
3. **t=135.9s** — `HEAD`/`GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` to **72.5.43.29:80**, User-Agent `Microsoft BITS/7.8` — a BITS job fetches a 159,232-byte PE32+ DLL (MZ header, "This program cannot be run in DOS mode").
4. **t=196.8s → end of capture (~1927s)** — sustained beaconing: hundreds of `GET /` and 3 `POST /` requests to 72.5.43.29:80, each carrying encrypted binary data in a `Cookie:` header (and POST body), with the spoofed IE6 User-Agent. Most get `400 Bad Request` in reply, consistent with a live C2 rejecting malformed/mistimed check-ins while still confirming the channel is active. This single conversation totals 3,497 frames / 865 KB, the largest external conversation in the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **72.5.43.29:80** | Sustained encrypted GET/POST "/" beaconing (tcp.stream 134, 142–166+), spoofed UA, `Cookie`-borne ciphertext, BITS-fetched DLL from same host |
| Domain | **quote.checkfedexexp.com** | Resolved via DNS (frames 6200–6413) to 104.21.55.70/172.67.170.159; served the malicious ZIP |
| Domain | **business.checkfedexexp.com** | 2 DNS queries from victim, same phishing infrastructure as quote.checkfedexexp.com (context/same campaign, no direct HTTP content observed) |
| URL | `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` | Frame 6418, HTTP GET, returned the Invoice ZIP |
| URL | `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | Frames 10611/10614, BITS-driven HEAD/GET, returned the second-stage DLL |
| File name | `Invoice 876597035_003.zip` | Content-Disposition header on frame 6404 response |
| File hash (SHA256) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Computed on the exported ZIP object |
| File name | `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | Filename inside the ZIP's central directory; obfuscated JS downloader |
| File hash (SHA256) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Computed on the JS file extracted from the ZIP |
| File hash (SHA256) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | Computed on the PE32+ DLL fetched from 72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 |

## Benign Context (not indicators)

- Microsoft/Windows telemetry, Office, SmartScreen, WNS, BITS delivery from legitimate `*.microsoft.com`/`*.msn.com`/Akamai/Azure CDN endpoints (23.x, 20.x, 13.x, 52.x, 204.79.197.x, 199.232.210.172 for the *legitimate* `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` BITS jobs).
- `www.bing.com`, `edgeservices.bing.com`, MSN endpoints — Edge browser default homepage/telemetry.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` — Adobe update check.
- `wpad.lafontainebleu.org`, `_ldap._tcp...lafontainebleu.org`, `_kerberos._tcp...` — normal AD/WPAD discovery traffic for the domain.
- SSDP `M-SEARCH` to 239.255.255.250:1900 — normal Windows network device discovery.
- `oneocsp.microsoft.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com` — OS certificate revocation / connectivity checks.

## Incident Summary

The Windows workstation DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as domain user `plucero` on lafontainebleu.org, was infected after browsing to a Cloudflare-fronted fake FedEx invoice site (`quote.checkfedexexp.com`) and downloading a ZIP containing a heavily obfuscated JavaScript downloader. The JS pulled a second-stage PE64 DLL via a spoofed Microsoft BITS job from 72.5.43.29, which then served as the malware's live command-and-control endpoint, receiving encrypted HTTP GET/POST check-ins from the host for the remainder of the capture. The behavior (invoice-themed ZIP lure, BITS-delivered DLL, encrypted Cookie-based HTTP C2 to a bare IP) is consistent with Latrodectus, though this attribution is behavioral rather than signature-confirmed.
